I am looking for a nice mechanical watch I can wear on special occasions, I don't need it to keep perfect time and I don't want to have to worry about a battery. I tried getting advice on reddit but the sub over there is really snotty and uppity.. anyway I'm hoping that with a smaller user base you guys can help me out :)

I'm sure we'd all love yo help here, but we'll need some more information first. Most important is price range. Are you looking to spend maybe a few hundred dollars (or less) or well into the thousands? Secondly, are you looking for a watch that is purely for dress occasions, or do you want something that can be easily dressed up with the potential to dress down? Answer those and you'll get much better recommendations! :)

I'm looking in the 400-700ish range no more than 1000. I have an old Gruen watch that my Uncle found at a garage sale and gave to me... Im pretty sure its not an expensive watch but I am pretty ignorant when it comes to watches. From a distance it looks like a nice gold watch, it has a decent weight to it but the clasp says made in china soooo yea.

Anyway I have a digital watch I wear daily so this would be worn with dress attire only. The reason I want strictly mechanical is so I don't have to worry about a battery.

In that price range, my personal recommendations would be to go with the Japanese offerings from Seiko and Orient. The Seiko 5 watches are definitely top bang-per-buck, but their selection of watches is not as expansive as Orient's. They do have dress watches, but most are stainless steel bands and you'd have to get your own leather strap to put it on. Orient has a wide selection of designs, including the dressy look you're after, but for higher prices than the Seikos.

My current dress watch is the Orient 60th Anniversary watch, which I find fits that perfect dress-watch look without being obnoxiously expensive. You can get similar watches, such as the Bambino, in the $200 price range.

Once caveat about the Orient watches is that they save money by not having hand-windable or hackable movements in their automatic watches, so when you take it out for dress occasions, you have to shake it lightly a few times to charge up the mainspring a bit so the watch will run. Then you can set the watch and put it on and the automatic movement charges it the rest of the way.

If you want to pay a bit more, you could go for the OrientStar el05004w, which costs more ($650 before discounts), but has a higher quality movement, is hand-windable, and hackable as well.

If you want to go for something higher-end in that price range, you might also want to look into vintage watches. You can grab decent 60s and 70s watches in your price-range from Swiss watchmakers. You can find hundreds of Omega Seamasters and Constellations alone on auction sites. Of course, buying vintage can be riskier, and you might need to get your watch serviced, but you can definitely get some high-quality pieces for a really good price that way.

Then again, you may hate all my suggestions. Either way, good luck with your watch selection!

I'm a tea noobie with a taste for loose leaf teas. So far my favorite is Root Beer Rooibos from Teaguys. The Rooibos is so fine that it slips through most of my infusers and ends up in my tea. Teavana's PerfectTea Maker works well without letting leaves through, but it's tougher to wash and isn't suited to one-cup-at-a-time brewing. I've tried single-cup infusers from FORLIFE and Schefs, which are easier to clean but are not fine enough to keep Rooibos leaves out of my tea.

I'm looking at getting this mesh single-cup infuser from Prepworks and this french press from Grosche, but I'm wondering what suggestions /v/tea has for infusing fine leaf tea. Thank you very much and happy brewing!
Best infuser for fine loose leaf teas (like Rooibos)?

I have the mesh single-cup infuser and it works very well. I use it for some of my finer teas (such as my mint green) which always seem to fall through the holes in other infusers.

It's also great for making iced tea in larger portions. It clips onto the side of your pitcher or mug which makes it really easy.

Cool, I might just order this one then :) I like single-cup infusers because they're easier to clean than the Teavana teamaker, but so far I haven't found any that are fine enough for my tea. This looks like it may be just the thing I'm looking for. Thanks for the perspective!
Something like this should work great for rooibois and other fine teas.

to follow up on this post, I ended up going with the french press from Garoshe and it's exactly what I was looking for. It's a little on the small side, but it's much easier to handwash than my PerfecTea Maker and I like pressing down the handle to filter the tea. As for the filter itself, it works at least as well as the PerfecTea Maker and there's no tea in my teeth, even using fine loose leaf tea like my rooibos. I'm thinking about going with a similar tea setup at work. Thank you very much for your suggestions and happy brewing!
